Summary for the user.

All 17 test cases pass, and `gofmt`/`go vet` are clean.

## What I did

Rewrote `markdown.go` (the only file changed) as a line-based parser, replacing the original character-scanning loop that threaded four pieces of state (`header`, `he`, `list`, `listOpened`) through one tangled loop with `pos += 2` skips and `LastIndex` comparisons.

The new structure:

- **`Render`** splits the input into lines and dispatches each to a helper. The only state left is `inList`, which controls when to open/close the `<ul>` around consecutive list items.
- **`headerLevel`** counts the *leading* run of `#` — 1–6 makes a header, anything else (including 7+) falls through to a paragraph. This naturally handles the "h7 is a paragraph" and "markdown symbols in header text" cases without the original's `he` flag and `header--` compensation trick.
- **`renderHeader` / `renderListItem` / `renderParagraph`** each render one line shape; markdown symbols inside the text stay literal because only line *prefixes* determine structure.
- **`renderEmphasis`** keeps the original's first-occurrence `__`/`_` replacement, now applied per line instead of across the whole document.

Refactoring notes are in comments on `Render`, per the spec's suggestion. `markdown_test.go` was not touched, and no new files were created.
